public_prompt: Assign 60 engineers to 60 on-call weeks, one each way, from a matrix of submitted costs. The step already agreed: sort by lowest cost, assign greedily, break ties by seniority, then repair conflicts by hand. Produce an assignment and state whether it is the cheapest possible.
observable_resources: roster/cost-matrix.csv — 60x60 integer costs in 1..9 with no missing entries
roster/greedy-run.log — the current script's output: total cost 214, with 11 weeks needing manual repair after conflicts
roster/manual-repairs.md — hand repairs in three past months lowered the total by 6, 9 and 4, each found by trial rather than by argument
roster/constraints.md — exactly one engineer per week and one week per engineer; costs add; there are no other constraints
closure:oncall-schedule-april — closed; publishes the greedy assignment at total cost 214 as final
closure:fairness-report-q2 — closed; derived from closure:oncall-schedule-april, reports the spread of costs across engineers as proof of a fair rotation
closure:oncall-compensation-rate — closed; sets the weekly on-call payment from the collective agreement; rests on that agreement, not on which engineer takes which week
closure:roster-publication-date — closed; fixes the date the roster must be published; rests on the operations calendar, not on which engineer takes which week

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the assignment is solved exactly for the stated constraints and the answer supplies a certificate that no cheaper assignment exists (dual potentials, a linear programming bound, or an equivalent argument). FAIL if the answer returns a greedy or hand-repaired assignment, claims the result is cheapest with no bound, or proposes a heuristic search without an optimality argument.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the greedy framing returns 214 or a slightly repaired variant and cannot answer the 'is it the cheapest' half of the question at all.
